subject: Helix Health - regional processing, subprocessors, and evidence
messages:
From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@helixhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal SecOps <secops@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T16:12:00Z
Subject: Request: where Helix data is processed + subprocessor evidence

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking this — we’re evaluating Redwood for some patient-facing features and need to confirm a few things before we advance to procurement. High-level questions below: 

1) For the hosted API, where is inference executed for EU customers? Which cloud regions/subprocessors will process or temporarily hold PII?
2) Do you have a mapping of subprocessors (compute, storage, monitoring) by region and the cross-border routes between them?
3) Can you commit to “EU-only processing” for a dataset containing EU resident PII if we specify region preference? If not, what parts (logs/control plane/metrics) might travel to the US?
4) Deletion/retention: do you provide an immediate deletion API and what is your backup retention policy? How long until complete purge?
5) Evidence: SOC 2 Type II, SCCs, dataflow diagram — can you share artifacts we can attach to our privacy review?

We’re on a tight timeline; a single doc with region-by-region subprocessor mapping plus the evidence would be ideal.

Thanks,
Chris Nolan
Security & Compliance Lead
Helix Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Legal SecOps <secops@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T20:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: where Helix data is processed + subprocessor evidence

Hi Chris — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary to get you started; I’m attaching a region/subprocessor matrix and our SCC/evidence bundle for your privacy team. I’ll loop in our privacy and solutions engineers on day two to address any deep technical follow-ups.

Quick answers:
- Hosted (default): inference is executed in the selected region: EU customers routed to europe-west1 (GCP) and eu-central-1 (AWS) depending on capacity.
- Dedicated: can be provisioned in a pinned region (EU-only) on dedicated GPU hosts.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-controlled; no Redwood control plane access unless explicitly enabled.

Subprocessors (summary):
- Compute: GCP (europe-west1), AWS (eu-central-1/us-east-1), Azure partner (w. europe) — see attached matrix for full list and roles.
- Storage: object stores colocated with compute region; backups encrypted and geo-redundant by default for hosted.
- Control plane/telemetry: control plane is hosted in us-central by default for operational reasons; metrics/alerts can be configured to exclude PII and retention can be reduced or disabled for EU-only contracts.

Cross-border handling:
- We rely on SCCs + contractual DPA. For Hosted customers who require EU-only commitments, we offer Dedicated or Private options.
- For telemetry that leaves the EU (metrics/alerts), we can provide minimized retention, pseudonymization, or contractual guarantees depending on the engagement.

Deletion + retention:
- Deletion API: yes (immediate logical delete).
- Backup purge: typically a 30-day window for snapshots/backups; we can shorten for Dedicated/Private under contract.
- Default log retention: 30 days (configurable).

Attachments included: redwood_region_subprocessor_matrix.xlsx, redwood_sccs_and_evidence.pdf, helix_dataflow_diagram.png (draft).

Next steps: 1) I’ll loop in Marissa (Privacy) and Jordan (Solutions) to provide a more granular subprocessor breakdown and to discuss contractual tweaks (e.g., no-US-access clause). 2) If useful, we can set a short technical call tomorrow.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@helixhealth.com>

Date: 2026-08-19T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: where Helix data is processed + subprocessor evidence

Hi Naomi — received, thanks. A few clarifying points from our privacy team: 

- We need confirmation that EU PII used for inference will not be accessible from US-based operator accounts (even for debugging). If the control plane is in the US, can you describe what operator access looks like and whether it can be restricted or logged to EU auditors?
- Deletion SLA: immediate logical delete is fine; we need the maximum time to physical purge from backups — you mentioned 30 days, can that be reduced to 7 for a clinical dataset?
- KV/cache: does the runtime write caches or KV data outside the chosen inference region? Any transient token logs?
- Subprocessor list: your matrix is useful, but can Marissa call out which subprocessors have the ability to decrypt customer data (if any) and which use customer-managed keys?

If you can add short answers inline and confirm availability for a 45-minute call tomorrow afternoon (UTC), that would be great.

—Chris

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Legal SecOps <secops@helixhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-19T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: where Helix data is processed + subprocessor evidence

Thanks — looping in Marissa (Privacy) and Jordan (Solutions) to address the specifics below. Short answers from the team are included; Marissa will follow with a marked-up matrix and operator-access controls.

Marissa (privacy) — short answers:
- Operator access & control plane: control plane incident ops live in us-central; operator accounts do not have default access to customer plaintext data. Access to payloads or customer-hosted inference state requires an explicit, auditable escalation (role-based access with JIT approvals). For EU-only commitments, we offer Dedicated or Private deployments that eliminate US-based operator access.
- Backup purge SLA: by standard policy hosted backups are purged within 30 days. For Helix Health we can contractually reduce that to 7 days for specific clinical datasets as part of a Dedicated commitment or under an elevated Enterprise DPA addendum.
- Subprocessor decryption capability: subprocessors that store encrypted backups have zero-knowledge storage by default; decryption keys are only accessible to Redwood’s KMS in hosted deployments. Customer-managed keys (CMKs) are supported for Dedicated/Private, which prevents Redwood staff or subprocessors from decrypting content. Marissa will flag which subprocessors support CMK.

Jordan (solutions) — runtime/KV/cache specifics:
- KV/cache: runtime maintains ephemeral KV caches in the same region as inference. By default caches are in-region and cleared per session; long-term stores (e.g., embeddings cache) are kept per customer policy and can be pinned to EU-only storage.
- Transient logs/tokens: we intentionally avoid logging raw request payloads; request/response payloads are treated as customer data and subject to the deletion API. Short-lived telemetry used for autoscaling (latency histograms, token counts) is aggregated and can be configured to omit identifiers.

Attachments we’ve re-attached: redwood_region_subprocessor_matrix.xlsx (we’ll send a version with subprocessors marked for CMK support), redwood_sccs_and_evidence.pdf (SOC2 + SCC summary), helix_dataflow_diagram.png (annotated draft).

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa to send a marked matrix with explicit CMK support and subprocessors that have decryption capability (expected by EOD tomorrow).
2) Draft DPA addendum with 7-day backup purge option for the clinical dataset (legal to produce within 3 business days).
3) 45-minute technical + privacy call tomorrow 15:00–15:45 UTC — confirm availability and I’ll send an invite.

Best regards,

Redwood Inference
